title: The Full basket of apples
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：full　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 full 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the keeper wrote of ① a full basket of apples in the calendar, and everybody in the tower said at once that it was ② fuller than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the keeper, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the full ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the fullest basket of apples anybody in the tower had ever seen, or so the calendar for January 1975 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too full to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the traveller who had come to help; the full ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a full account of the journey, and said that no traveller in his right mind would call it ⑥ as full as the account of the journey they had once had in the old tower. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was full or not, and he said so.

By 1988 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the calendar. What the line asked for was ⑦ something full, and nothing besides. The traveller from the next tower called the whole plan ⑧ quite full; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the calendar kept the names of the full ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1991, before dawn, she wrote of another full basket of apples in the same calendar, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ fuller than anybody had expected. ⑩ The fullest account of the journey in the whole tower, she said in 1993, was the one she could never quite name; the full ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 满（前置定语 a full basket of apples：1981 年守夜人在年历里记下的那件满的篮子）
B. adj. 满／完整（比较级 fuller than：文中两处，一处比装满苹果的篮子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 满／完整（最高级 the fullest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 满（表语 too full to do：母亲觉得它太满，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 完整（前置定语 a full account of the journey：叔叔把整件事称作一桩完整的旅行记录）
F. adj. 完整（同级比较 as full as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩完整的旅行记录相比）
G. adj. 完整（后置定语 something full：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 完整（受程度副词修饰 quite full：那位过路人的评价）

items.q: the fullest basket of apples anybody
a full account of the journey
The fullest account of the journey in

answers.why: full 意为“满”，1981 年守夜人在年历里记下的是“一件满的篮子”，此处作前置定语 a full basket of apples。
full 意为“满”，此处用比较级 fuller than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
full 意为“满”，年历上 一月 那行字说它是钟楼里最满的一件，故用最高级 the fullest basket of apples。
full 意为“满”，母亲认为这件东西“太满了，谁也用不上”，too full to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
full 意为“完整”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩完整的旅行记录”，此处作前置定语 a full account of the journey。
full 意为“完整”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩完整的旅行记录一样完整”，同级比较用 as full as。
full 意为“完整”，年历上那半行字要的是“完整的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something full。
full 意为“完整”，邻钟楼来的那位过路人认为这套计划“相当完整”，quite 修饰原级 full。
full 意为“完整”，1991 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要完整”，故用比较级 fuller than。
full 意为“完整”，母亲 1993 年说的是“整个钟楼里最完整的那一桩”，故用最高级 the fullest account of the journey。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1981 年，守夜人在年历里记下了一件满的篮子。（a full basket of apples）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更满。（fuller than …）
母亲觉得它太满，谁也用不上。（too full to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩完整的旅行记录。（a full account of the journey）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩完整的旅行记录一样完整。（as full as …）
到了 1988 年，年历上只剩半行字：要的是一件完整的东西。（something full）
answers: In 1981 the keeper wrote of a full basket of apples in the calendar.
Everybody said it was fuller than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too full to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a full account of the journey.
He said nobody would call it as full as the account of the journey they had once had.
By 1988 the calendar asked for nothing but something full.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 full 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1981 the keeper wrote of a full basket of apples in the calendar, and nobody forgot it.
It was the fullest basket of apples in the tower, or so the calendar says.
My mother thought it too full to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a full account of the journey, and nobody argued with him.
The traveller from the next tower called the plan quite full, and everybody laughed.
The full ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
